title: Standard Contract Rules — Mia Lee Illustration LLC

blocks.text: Revision Cap Rule (constraint_A)

All contracts must cap client revisions at two (2) rounds per project stage (e.g., sketch stage, color stage, final stage). Any revision request beyond the two-round cap triggers a mandatory change-order fee billed at $150/hour. No exceptions without written sign-off from Mia. Contracts that include unlimited revision language or omit a revision cap entirely are a hard red-line and must not be signed as presented.
50% Deposit Rule
All new project contracts require a 50% deposit paid before work begins. Deposit is non-refundable after sketch approval.
Change-Order Fee Trigger

Scope changes beyond the agreed deliverables list, additional revision rounds beyond the cap, or deadline compression requests after contract signing all trigger a change-order. Change-orders must be documented in writing and signed by both parties before additional work proceeds.
Kill Fee
If a project is cancelled by the client after sketch approval, a 25% kill fee applies on the remaining balance.

title: Standard Contract Rules — Mia Lee Illustration LLC

blocks.text: Standard Contract Rules — Mia Lee Illustration LLC
These rules are NON-NEGOTIABLE and apply to all new client contracts. Any incoming contract that violates a hard rule must be counter-proposed or declined before signing. Last reviewed: March 2026.
HARD RULES (Non-Negotiable)

RULE H-1 — 50% UPFRONT DEPOSIT: All commissions require a 50% deposit of the total agreed fee paid before any work commences (including sketches). No exceptions. Full payment-on-delivery contracts are not acceptable.

RULE H-2 — 3-STAGE GATE STRUCTURE: All illustration work proceeds through three mandatory approval gates: (1) Rough Sketch Approval — client approves direction before rendering begins; (2) Refined Sketch / Comp Review — client approves composition and detail before finals; (3) Final Delivery — client accepts finished art. Revisions are scoped to each stage. No stage may be skipped. Unlimited open-ended revision rights are not acceptable.

RULE H-3 — KILL FEE MINIMUM 25%: If a project is cancelled after commencement, the kill fee must be no less than 25% of the total contracted fee (not the remaining unpaid balance). Kill fees below this threshold are not acceptable.
RULE H-4 — PAYMENT TERMS MAX 30 DAYS: Final balance payment must be due within 30 days of final delivery acceptance. Net-60 or longer terms are not acceptable without a premium rate adjustment.
SOFT RULES (Standard Terms — Negotiable with Justification)

SOFT S-1 — PORTFOLIO DISPLAY RIGHTS: Mia Lee retains the right to display commissioned work in her portfolio (print and digital) and on social media for self-promotion purposes. Contracts that restrict portfolio display rights should be counter-proposed to include a standard portfolio clause. Acceptable to waive only for high-value confidential projects with a rate premium.

SOFT S-2 — CREDIT LINE FORMAT: Standard credit line is 'Illustrations © Mia Lee / Mia Lee Illustration LLC'. Credit as 'Illustrations by Mia Lee' (without copyright symbol or LLC attribution) is acceptable for editorial interiors but should be flagged and negotiated where possible.

SOFT S-3 — IP LICENSING SCOPE: Mia Lee's standard terms grant non-exclusive rights for the specific commissioned use (e.g., book interior, one edition). Worldwide perpetual exclusive rights, merchandise rights, and derivative works rights require a separate licensing fee or rate uplift of at least 30%. Full IP assignment (work-for-hire) is acceptable only at a significant rate premium.

SOFT S-4 — DERIVATIVE WORKS: Publisher rights to create derivative works from commissioned illustrations (e.g., merchandise, adaptations) must be separately negotiated and compensated. Blanket derivative works rights in a base commission contract should be flagged.
Response Protocol
If any HARD RULE is violated: do not sign. Issue a redline counter-proposal addressing all hard conflicts. If client refuses to negotiate hard rules, decline the contract.
If only SOFT RULES are at issue: negotiate in good faith. Document all deviations from standard terms in the client log.
Response window: aim to return counter-proposals within 48 hours of receiving an incoming contract.

title: Standard Contract Rules — Mia Lee Illustration LLC

blocks.text: Non-Negotiable Rules (apply to all client contracts)

1. 50% deposit required before any work begins. No exceptions. Deposit is non-refundable once work commences.
2. Scope is fixed at contract signing. Any additions — regardless of how they are framed by the client — require a written amendment with adjusted fee and timeline before additional work begins.
3. Revision rounds are capped per contract. Additional rounds are billed at the hourly rate specified in the contract.
4. Delivery deadlines are contingent on scope remaining as signed. Client-initiated scope additions automatically extend the delivery timeline unless the amendment explicitly waives the extension.
5. No work on out-of-scope items until amendment is countersigned. Verbal or email agreements do not constitute amendments.
Scope Creep Response Protocol

When a client requests additions after contract signing:
1. Do not agree verbally or by email without a formal amendment.
2. Acknowledge the request warmly and reference the contract scope.
3. Prepare a written amendment with: (a) description of additional deliverable, (b) additional fee, (c) revised delivery timeline.
4. Send amendment for countersignature before beginning any additional work.
5. Log the request and response in the client's Notion log.

title: Client Log — Greenfield Press (ACTIVE — canonical record as of 2026-04-22) — Clause 4b Reimbursement Rules

blocks.text: Clause 4b — Reimbursable Supply & Materials Rules (Spring 2026 Contract)

Greenfield Press will reimburse Mia Lee Illustration LLC for project-specific art supplies and materials directly consumed in the production of contracted deliverables (3 cover variations, Spring 2026), subject to the following conditions and exclusions.
Reimbursable Items (clause 4b eligible)

items: Professional-grade paints, inks, and pigments purchased specifically for named deliverables (cover variations 1, 2, 3)
Professional-grade brushes and applicators required for the contracted finish/medium specified in the project brief
Archival or professional-grade paper and illustration board purchased for final artwork production (not drafting or sketching)
Mixed-media materials (acrylic inks, gouache, watercolor) where the medium is specified in the approved project brief

blocks.text: Non-Reimbursable Items (clause 4b exclusions)

items: General-purpose sketchbooks, sketch pads, and bulk paper pads (including but not limited to Canson XL, Strathmore 400 series sketch pads, and equivalent student/general-use formats)
Studio overhead supplies not tied to a specific named deliverable
Discretionary studio stock items purchased for general inventory
Items purchased primarily to meet vendor order minimums or discount thresholds rather than for direct project use
Pencils, erasers, and drafting tools used for preliminary sketching (considered standard studio overhead)

blocks.text: Reimbursement Process

Submit itemized receipts with project attribution notes to dana.whitfield@greenfieldpress.example within 30 days of purchase. Use reimbursement tracker WB-7/WB-8 to log submissions. Greenfield processes reimbursements on Net-30 from receipt of claim.

⚠️ IMPORTANT: Canson XL Sketchbook Pad (large format) is explicitly non-reimbursable under clause 4b. It falls under 'general-purpose sketchbooks and bulk paper pads.' Do not include in reimbursement claims. If currently in Blick cart as threshold filler, remove before order submission.
Clause 4b Reimbursement Cap

Total reimbursable supplies capped at $200 for the Spring 2026 engagement (3 cover variations). Mia must pre-approve any single-item purchase over $75 with Dana Whitfield before purchase to ensure reimbursement eligibility.
